findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value changed from 4 to 3, repurposing 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED
findings.body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the previously-used value 4 is now repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED. Anyone who has already scripted around the previous exit-code contract (where 4 meant 'recreate upgrade required') will now get a different, incompatible meaning for the same exit code. Even though the docs for this preview tool already described code 3 for recreate-required (meaning the running implementation and docs were previously inconsistent), this PR silently changes the runtime behavior of an already-usable CLI command. Given the documentation explicitly instructs consumers to rely on the exit code contract ('they should rely only on the exit code of the check command'), this is a user-facing behavioral change that should be called out clearly in release notes / changelog, not just silently fixed.

findings.title: Feature key hardcoded as string literal instead of using the Feature enum
findings.body: printFeatureDisabled() hardcodes the string 'rolling-updates' in the error message instead of referencing Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(). If the feature's enum name or generated key is ever changed, this message will silently become inconsistent with the actual required feature flag, misleading users on how to enable the feature.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the exit code
findings.body: The new test testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the printed error message but never verifies that the command exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which is the actual contract this PR introduces/relies on (also documented in update-compatibility.adoc). Without an exit-code assertion, a regression that changes or removes the picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) call in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata would not be caught by this test.

findings.title: CAUTION block wording overstates scope of failure
findings.body: The CAUTION note states 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail,' which reads as if the entire Operator stops working without this feature. Based on the accompanying NOTE and the UpgradeTest.java changes (where the default/null update-strategy path does not enable the rolling-updates feature and still works, mimicking old behavior), the feature is only required when the update.strategy field is explicitly configured. The CAUTION text should clarify that only configuring spec.update.strategy requires the feature, to avoid readers believing they must always enable the preview feature flag for the Operator to function at all.
